archetypes.name: phase-contract
archetypes.rationale: Targets the new phase-driver boundary where KV names, result-env allowlists, exit codes, and orchestrator reads can drift from the existing rank-1 convention.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed design-route and design-init-runparams contracts line up with the existing lib-phase-driver convention, result-env writing/reading, emit_kv stdout usage, and SKILL.md consumer flow. Pay special attention to ROUTE and INIT_STATUS enums, allowlisted KVs, atomic env output, symlink refusal, and whether cancel verdicts remain non-failures. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-anchor
archetypes.rationale: The plan intentionally avoids new harnesses, so the main risk is under-specified re-pointing of existing structure and replica tests.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the planned updates to scripts/test-design-structure.sh and scripts/test-step0b-router-flag-recovery.sh are sufficient to pin the behavior being moved out of SKILL.md. Look for plan holes where ordering, warning literals, jq merge semantics, manual flag handling, title filtering, resume loading, or env refresh behavior could regress without a failing test. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: orchestrator-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The split is organized around LLM/user gates, making misplaced responsibilities between scripts and the orchestrator a high-value plan defect target.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the plan for boundary mistakes between deterministic driver scripts and the Step 0b orchestrator. Focus on clarify and already-planned AskUserQuestion gates, verbal issue creation, cancel banners, Final summary handling, resume STEP=0c flow, and feature-description ownership. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
